This section details how a backdoor could be done securely.

A quick summary of the two main types of cryptography:

  • Public key crypto has two keys: a public key and a private key. Information encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted by the private key. It cannot be decrypted with the public key.
  • Symmetric crypto has one key. Information encrypted with the key can only be decrypted with that same key.

Public key crypto is very slow, so frequently a session key is generated which is used to encrypt the message with symmetric crypto. The session key is then the only part encrypted with the public key crypto. This encrypted session key is then transported along with the message. When decrypting, you first decrypt the session key, then you use that session key to decrypt the rest of the message.

A backdoor would simply have the session key encrypted by the NSA's public key and sent with the message along with the other encrypted session key. An attacker could attack either one of the two encrypted keys in order to decrypt the message. This is not the weak point.

Now the problem is that the more you use a key, the more you expose that key. If Apple or Google is decrypting a hundred messages a day with their backdoor key, eventually a mistake will be made, and the key would be exposed. Once that backdoor key is exposed, their is no hiding it again. If we know about the loss; the cost would be astronomical as all past messages could now be decrypted by the malicious actor. If we don't know about the loss, the cost would be even greater, as current and future messages would be exposed as well.

By building in a back door, you've built a multi-trillion dollar weak point in your software. It would be pretty safe to assume that China or Russia would be willing to spend tens or hundreds of millions to get that key. If you are part of the team responsible for keeping that key safe, would you turn down a $50 million bribe?
